What goes into
the website.

We agree the pages, features, content responsibilities and review stages in your proposal. The scope fits the project, whether it is one page or several.

Page planning

A structure that helps visitors find your services, understand your business and take the next step.

Visual design

Type, colour, images and layouts that give the website a consistent identity.

Responsive build

Layouts for phones and larger screens, with readable text and usable controls.

Contact routes

The agreed contact actions, including tested delivery when a form is part of the scope.

SEO foundations

Page titles, descriptions, headings, image optimisation and technical indexing checks for the agreed pages.

Review & handover

Feedback at agreed stages, key-flow checks and an explanation of editing and ownership.

SEO foundations are part of the build. Ongoing SEO campaigns, advertising and social media management are separate disciplines and are not included.

Before we begin

A few useful
things to know.

You can start with a business description, an existing website if you have one, and the result you want visitors to find.

Do you offer SEO or digital marketing?

Our website builds include agreed SEO foundations, such as page titles, headings, image optimisation and technical indexing checks. We do not currently offer ongoing SEO campaigns, paid advertising or social media management. Search visibility and enquiries are not guaranteed.

Do I need finished content?

No. We can begin with an outline. The scope identifies who prepares the final words and images, when they are needed and who approves them. You confirm the business information and rights to supplied material.

Can I update the website myself?

We discuss what you need to edit before choosing the platform. Editing access, instructions and any ongoing support are agreed as part of the project.

How much does it cost, and how long does it take?

The fee and schedule follow the scope. Pages, features, existing setup, content and feedback all affect the work, so those dependencies are included in the proposal.

Who owns the website and accounts?

File ownership, domain and hosting accounts, licences and access handover are agreed before work starts. Any third-party restrictions and recurring charges are identified separately.
